Build Quality-Control Settings from a Preset

Source: R/qc_config.R
qc_config.Rd

Build the set of quality-control (QC) thresholds used by the whole pipeline. Start from a preset with profile and override any parameter through ....

qc_config(profile = c("casey", "national", "legacy"), ...)

Arguments

profile

Preset to start from:

  • "casey" (default): feeder error criteria of Casey et al. (2005), robust regression (MASS::rlm) for body weight outliers and a quadratic growth curve.

  • "national": the national FCR procedure (chapter 6, "FCR raw data processing"): rlm weights <= 0.25 removed, whole days whose records all have rlm weights < 0.90 removed, daily weight = mean weighted by the rlm weights, pigs with a daily-weight R² < 0.995 (quadratic) or more than 10% of days without feed removed, 10 kg weight classes checked and FCR from cumulative feed intake (method = "national"). Feed errors and their correction are those of the package.

  • "legacy": STL + robust regression + robust SD outlier detection and a Gompertz growth curve.

...

Parameters to override, as name = value. See Parameters.

Value

An object of class ppt_qc: a named list of parameters with the preset name in attribute "profile".

Parameters

Method

  • method: "standard" (default): FCR = ADFI / ADG over the stage; "national": FCR from the cumulative feed intake between the stage limits, with the weight-class checks of the national procedure (see calc_fcr()).

Station transfer (pigs seen at several stations)

  • max_gap_days: maximum gap between two stations to treat the pig as transferred. A larger gap splits it into two animals. Default 3.

  • max_overlap_days: maximum time overlap between two stations. A larger overlap is treated as transponder misreads. Default 1.

  • max_jump_kg: body weight jump at the transfer that triggers a warning. Default 10.

Body weight records

  • weight_range: valid body weight of a single record, kg.

  • adapt_days: adaptation period after entry, days (default 7). Body weights of the first adapt_days days after a pig's first visit are not used (qc_flag = "adaptation"). Its feed intake is kept: it counts for ADFI and FCR when these days lie inside stage_range (e.g. a pig that enters at 45 kg with a 30-120 kg stage), and not when the pig is still below the stage. 0 = off.

  • weight_outlier: one or more of "rlm", "loess", "stl", "sd".

  • outlier_combine: "any" (outlier for any method) or "majority".

  • rlm_cutoff: records with a robust regression weight below this are outliers (at or below with method = "national"). Default 0.5.

  • day_weight_min: optional, a day on which every record has an rlm weight below this is removed as a whole (qc_flag = "day_weight"; national: 0.90). Needs "rlm" in weight_outlier. NULL = off.

  • daily_weight: daily body weight from the valid records: "median" (default) or "weighted_mean" (mean weighted by the rlm weights, national).

  • sd_max: residuals beyond this many robust SDs (MAD) are outliers.

  • loess_span: smoothing span for LOESS. Default 0.75.

  • rel_dev_max: optional, relative deviation from the curve above which a record is an outlier (e.g. 0.25). NULL = off.

  • daily_drop_min: optional, a day whose weight is below this ratio of the previous day is an outlier (e.g. 0.90). NULL = off.

  • weight_track: track the weight of each pig back from the end of the test (default TRUE). The scale only counts a pig standing on it with all four feet, so a reading is too light only rarely, while several small pigs on the scale at once give readings that are too heavy. At the end of the test the pigs are large and only one fits on the scale, so the last days are the most reliable. Starting from the median of the last 3 recorded days and the daily gain of the last 14 days, the weight is tracked back day by day: a record is kept when it lies within track_tol (default 8%, at least 2 kg, widened by 0.5 kg per day without kept records) of the weight expected for that day; the daily gain is updated from the kept daily weights of the next 10 days. Other records are removed (qc_flag = "track"). The outlier methods (weight_outlier) do not remove kept records, since a smooth curve cannot follow e.g. slow growth for weeks after entry; they are used for pigs that are not tracked (less than 7 recorded days or a test shorter than 14 days) and when weight_track = FALSE.

Pig-level checks

  • min_test_days, min_records: minimum test length (days) and number of valid weight records.

  • max_missing_rate: maximum share of days without a valid weight.

  • daily_r2_min: optional, pigs whose daily weights fit a quadratic curve with an R² below this are removed (national: 0.995). NULL = off.

  • max_feed_missing: optional, pigs without any feed record on more than this share of their test days are removed (national: 0.10). NULL = off.

  • entry_weight_max, exit_weight_min: maximum entry and minimum exit body weight, kg.

  • curve_r2_min: optional, pigs whose growth curve R² is below this are flagged as low confidence (not removed). NULL = off.

  • max_daily_jump_kg: optional, pigs whose daily median weight changes by more than this many kg per day between consecutive days are flagged as low confidence (not removed). NULL = off.

  • track_flag_share: pigs whose tracking removes more than this share of their records are flagged as low confidence: the scale probably did not weigh them correctly for a long time (e.g. a faulty load cell). Default 0.4.

Growth and ADG

  • stage_range: body weight interval for ADG and FCR, kg.

  • curve_model: "poly1", "poly2", "poly3", "loess" or "gompertz" (falls back to "poly2" when it does not converge).

  • adg_method: "lm" (default): ADG is the slope of a linear regression of all valid weight records between the stage start and end times (lm_slope; its R² is r_squared); "curve": ADG is the weight difference of the stage divided by the days the growth curve needs for it. Both are always reported (lm_slope, adg_curve). With "lm", a pig without enough records in the stage (< 5 records or < 7 days) gets the curve ADG (adg_source).

  • curve_margin_kg: optional, fit the growth curve only to the records around the stage: from the last day whose daily median weight is below stage_range[1] - curve_margin_kg to the first day above stage_range[2] + curve_margin_kg (cut by time, not by weight). Early weeks far below the stage (e.g. slow growth after entry) then no longer bend the curve. Falls back to all records when fewer than 10 records or 7 days remain. NULL (default) = all records; 5 is a sensible value.

  • max_extrap_days: maximum extrapolation of the curve, days.

Feeder errors (Casey et al. 2005, Table 3)

  • fiv_range: FIV-lo / FIV-hi, feed intake per visit, g.

  • fiv0_abs_max: FIV-0, maximum |FIV| for a 0 s visit, g.

  • duration_max: OTV-hi, maximum occupation time per visit, s.

  • speed_fiv_lo_max: FRV-hi-FIV-lo, maximum feeding rate for visits with 0 < FIV < 50 g, g/min.

  • speed_strict_max: FRV-hi-strict, maximum feeding rate when the preceding or following visit has FIV < -20 g, g/min.

  • speed_range: FRV-lo and FRV-hi, g/min.

  • idle_duration_max: FRV-0, maximum occupation time with no intake, s.

  • trough_diff_range: LWD / FWD, trough weight difference between subsequent visits, g.

  • max_unidentified_feed_kg: feed disappearance in unidentified visits per feeder above which a warning is given.

  • fiv_max_by_weight: optional table that replaces the upper limit of fiv_range (FIV-hi) by a limit that depends on body weight, and optionally on breed. Columns weight_from (kg, lower bound of the weight class), fiv_max (g) and optionally breed. See fiv_max_example(). NULL = off.

Daily feed intake

  • dfi_range: valid daily feed intake, kg.

  • dfi_quantile: optional, lower and upper quantile cut-offs (e.g. c(0.025, 0.99)). NULL = off.

  • dfi_correct: "lmm" (Jiao et al. 2014) or "none".

  • impute_method: "linear" (linear interpolation, LOESS for long gaps, intake ~ body weight regression at the stage ends), "loess" (robust LOESS over days everywhere) or "national" (gaps of up to long_gap_days days: LOESS over days; longer gaps: linear regression of intake on body weight).

  • long_gap_days: inside gaps longer than this many days are imputed with LOESS instead of a straight line (impute_method = "linear"), or by regression on body weight ("national", 3 days). Default 7.

Confidence flags (used by calc_fcr())

  • max_edge_extrap_days: a pig is "low_confidence" when the growth curve or the feed intake is extrapolated over more than this many days at the start or the end of the stage. Default 15.

  • min_coverage: minimum share of stage days with recorded feed intake. Default 0.7.

  • bin_width: width of the body weight classes used for the segment checks of calc_fcr(), kg. Default 10.

  • min_bin_coverage_kg: an inner weight class whose recorded body weights span less than this many kg flags the pig. Default 6.

  • bin_fcr_limits: optional table of plausible FCR per weight class, columns weight_from (kg), fcr_min, fcr_max. See bin_fcr_example(). NULL = off (national: table 5 of the procedure).

  • bin_min_gain_kg: national method: a weight class whose weight gain is below this is removed. Default 6.

  • cfi_r2_min: national method: pigs whose cumulative feed intake fits body weight (linear) with an R² at or below this are removed. Default 0.95.

References

Casey, D. S., Stern, H. S., & Dekkers, J. C. M. (2005). Identification of errors and factors associated with errors in data from electronic swine feeders. Journal of Animal Science, 83, 969-982.

Jiao, S., Maltecca, C., Gray, K. A., & Cassady, J. P. (2014). Feed intake, average daily gain, feed efficiency, and real-time ultrasound traits in Duroc pigs: I. Journal of Animal Science, 92, 2377-2386.
